# avahi / fuzz-domain

avahi's own fuzz target `fuzz-domain` ([source](source/fuzz-domain.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over avahi (avahi/avahi at b1a83592).

Checks 3 properties (listed below); the first, an invariant: normalization preserves identity: for a valid domain name s, avahi_domain_equal(s, normalize(s)) (label-wise unescape + case-insensitive compare).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against avahi at commit b1a83592.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- if the input is a valid domain name (avahi_is_valid_domain_name) then avahi_normalize_name_strdup must succeed ([lines 46-49](source/fuzz-domain.c#L46-L49)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.
- normalization preserves identity: for a valid domain name s, avahi_domain_equal(s, normalize(s)) (label-wise unescape + case-insensitive compare) ([lines 50-51](source/fuzz-domain.c#L50-L51)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.
- for ANY input whose normalization succeeds, avahi_domain_equal(s, normalize(s)) must hold ([lines 56-57](source/fuzz-domain.c#L56-L57)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.

A failure of the check at lines 56-57 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name it exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies it on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other checks.

## Statements ([Statements.v](Statements.v), [Characterise.v](Characterise.v), [Distribution.v](Distribution.v))

| statement | in one line | status |
|---|---|---|
| `plain_halts` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the check at lines 56-57 above holds | open |
| `ubsan_halts` | on every input on which the UBSan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the check at lines 56-57 above holds | open |
| `ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; UBSan never fires | open |
| `ubsan_disagrees_at_most` | P[plain and UBSan disagree] <= b under [Distribution.v](Distribution.v) | open (best proved b: none) |
| `ubsan_agreement_decidable` | some program decides exactly the inputs where plain and UBSan agree | open |

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch avahi` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz-domain.plain` | 56,968 | `90529935140f72988e9924c0176c756bd2da77e6e482ef1579b54d0370433a62` |
| ubsan | `fuzz-domain.ubsan` | 57,448 | `5de4b70136b61f37102acb55903c1ac25a2d87a4b29c9289af102cf86ccfb128` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
